title: $61,140 paper loss last week, and 227 option trades did $60,180 of it. The other 2,939 trades were nearly flat
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
Disclosure first: I built the desk this comes from, it's paper money, and there's no link in here.

Last week the house paper desk closed 3,166 trades between Monday 5 Oct and Friday 9 Oct and finished -$61,140. Splitting it by instrument is the reason for this post, because the split is not close at all:

| what | trades | paper P&L |
|---|---|---|
| option trades | 227 | -$60,180 |
| stock trades | 2,939 | -$960 |
| total | 3,166 | -$61,140 |

So 7% of the trades did 98% of the damage. Inside the options it's worse than the net suggests: 50 winners made +$24,913 and 177 losers gave back -$85,092.

By day, worst first:

| exit day | closed | paper P&L | of which options |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wed 10-07 | 706 | -$34,090 | -$34,034 |
| Thu 10-08 | 719 | -$15,650 | -$15,910 |
| Fri 10-09 | 478 | -$8,108 | -$9,416 |
| Tue 10-06 | 599 | -$3,625 | -$1,550 |
| Mon 10-05 | 664 | +$333 | +$730 |

The three worst single trades were all calls bought around 23-24 Sep and held about two weeks: a SanDisk call in at $71.10 and out at $0.95 (-$7,016), another SanDisk call in at $70.20 and out at $0.20 (-$7,001), and a Northrop call in at $71.70, out at $32.00 (-$3,971). The part that stings: the week before, one SanDisk call was the 3rd best of 3,674 trades at +$9,478. Same name, same kind of bet, one week apart.

I don't know yet why it was this lopsided. My first guess is sizing: a $70 call and a $3 call each count as "one position", and a share that drops 4% costs 4% while a call that drifts sideways for two weeks costs most of what you paid for it. I haven't checked that properly, so treat it as a guess.

One caveat: Friday's expiries hadn't all settled when I pulled this, so the Friday row may move a little on Monday's re-pull.

Since people here ask how I see this split at all: I built Quantradin (quantradin.com) for exactly this kind of check before a rule goes live. You describe the rule in plain words or paste Pine, it backtests with no look-ahead, and options fill at the real bid and ask, never the middle, so a call bought at $71 shows the price you'd actually have paid. Free and paper only.

For anyone here running an AI bot that trades both shares and options: how do you size the options side, a fixed dollar cap per trade, a share of the account, or something that looks at the premium itself
